audit.title: CCIP Service Limits

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Opens with a serviceable orientation sentence — "This section outlines the operational limits for Chainlink CCIP across different blockchain architectures." But the implied question ("what are the limits?") is deferred to sub-pages; no liftable answer lives here.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Clean — 1 H1, one coherent section, 4 descriptive bullets, 0 level skips. Fine for a hub, but no summary table where the highest-value extraction would occur.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak. 0 numerals with units, 0 version strings — a limits page with no limits. This is the dominant deficiency.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 5 internal links, all descriptive and correctly scoped; 0 external/primary sources. Adequate for a hub.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: No crisp one-liner defining "CCIP service limits" for verbatim lift.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: No JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no `datePublished`/`dateModified` in head (a body "Last Updated: 2025-09-03" exists but isn't machine-exposed). CLI should pass raw `<head>` to confirm.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code — not applicable for an index page; not penalized.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers the "index" intent only. Misses symptom/spec queries like "CCIP max message size," "CCIP rate limit per lane," "CCIP max data bytes."

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; no action needed. Consistent naming ("Chainlink CCIP"), no jargon debt.

audit.summary: This is a thin navigation hub that routes to four platform-specific CCIP service-limit pages (EVM, Solana, Aptos, network-specific). Its clearest strength is clean, unambiguous prose and a sensible link structure; its biggest weakness is that a page literally titled "Service Limits" contains **zero actual limit values** (83 words, 3 numerals, 0 with units) — so it cannot be retrieved or cited for any concrete "what is the max X" query, which is exactly how developers and agents ask about limits. As an index it works; as a citable answer it does not. The honest verdict: acceptable hub, but a missed opportunity to become the canonical liftable summary of CCIP's core limits.

recommendations.title: Add a cross-platform limits summary table
recommendations.where: After the intro sentence, before or replacing the bullet list.
recommendations.issue: Page titled "Service Limits" contains 0 limit values.
recommendations.change: Add a table with the handful of highest-traffic limits (e.g. max message data bytes, max token amounts per message, gas limit ceilings) per family, each row linking to the detailed sub-page. Even 5–8 canonical numbers make this page directly citable.
recommendations.why: Quantitative specifics are the highest-lift change; a limits hub with numbers becomes the retrievable answer instead of a dead-end redirect.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/spec-phrased headings
recommendations.issue: No headings match how limits are queried ("what is the maximum…").
recommendations.change: Add H2s like "What is the maximum CCIP message size?", "CCIP rate limits per lane", "Which chains have special limits?" — each answering in the first sentence then linking deeper.
recommendations.why: Devs/agents query by symptom and spec, not by "service limits" — question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses.

recommendations.title: Add a quotable canonical definition
recommendations.issue: No self-contained definition of "CCIP service limits."
recommendations.change: Lead with a crisp one-liner, e.g. "CCIP service limits are the per-message, per-lane, and per-network operational maximums (message size, token amounts, and rate limits) that Chainlink CCIP enforces on cross-chain transactions."
recommendations.why: A verbatim-liftable definition near first use outperforms diffuse pointer prose.

recommendations.title: Add TechArticle JSON-LD and canonical URL
recommendations.issue: JSON-LD 0 blocks, canonical MISSING, no machine dateModified.
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `dateModified: 2025-09-03`, `inLanguage`, and a self-referential canonical URL; expose the "Last Updated" as a machine-readable date.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and freshness signals raise parseability and E-E-A-T trust for agents.

recommendations.title: Link one external primary source
recommendations.change: Link the CCIP architecture/spec or best-practices page where limit rationale is defined.
recommendations.why: Primary-source links raise credibility and citation rate.

antiPatterns: **Title/content mismatch:** page named "Service Limits" states no limits — the main substantive gap, not stuffing or fluff.
No keyword stuffing, no marketing fluff, no unresolved cross-references, no ambiguous entities. Prose is clean.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced — good site-level signal; ensure it lists the sub-pages too.
Head metadata could not be verified from the provided content; CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a definitive read of canonical/schema/date tags.
Whether this hub or the deeper EVM/SVM/Aptos pages get cited is partly a site-internal-linking (canonical-hub) concern; ensure sub-pages link back up to this index.
